title: Mock 4 · Portfolio and Performance
blurb: Risk attitudes, asset allocation and a short Sharpe-vs-Treynor caselet, plus operational and regulatory basics across the syllabus.

questions.q: A technology-based solution that offers standardised model portfolios which clients or advisers can buy, monitor and review across products is called:
questions.explanation: Wraps and platforms are technology-based, standardised advisory solutions offering model portfolios; they may charge a fee and share it with the adviser using them.
hints: Fee-only planners give comprehensive advice and usually do not execute.
PMS is an individually managed portfolio service under separate SEBI regulations.

questions.q: Vikram borrows ₹4 lakh at 9% a year (monthly rests) and can pay ₹10,000 a month. Approximately how many months will it take to repay the loan?
questions.explanation: NPER(0.09/12, -10000, 400000) = 47.7 months, i.e. about 48 months.
hints: Too short: interest makes repayment take longer than 40 months.

questions.q: Which of the following holdings would the workbook count as a liquid asset when calculating the liquidity ratio?
options: A 5-year fixed deposit with 3 years to run
A bank fixed deposit maturing in 5 months
questions.explanation: Liquid assets include savings bank balances, FDs maturing within 6 months and liquid funds. Shares are excluded because their value can fluctuate; closed-end funds and long FDs are not easily realisable.
hints: Shares are excluded due to value uncertainty.
Closed-end units are not as easily realisable.
Long-term FDs are not liquid assets.

questions.q: Dev earns ₹15 lakh a year. His recurring annual expenses are ₹10.5 lakh. He takes a ₹4 lakh foreign holiday every 4 years, and this year also paid a one-time ₹1 lakh surgery bill. What is his expense ratio as per the workbook method?
questions.explanation: Periodic expenses are annualised (₹4 lakh / 4 = ₹1 lakh a year) and non-recurring items (the one-time surgery) are excluded. Expense ratio = (10.5 + 1) / 15 = 76.67%.
hints: This ignores the annualised holiday cost.
This also adds the one-time surgery, which should be excluded.
This adds the full ₹4 lakh holiday and the surgery.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a hire purchase agreement and a lease?
options: Under a lease the lessee becomes owner after the last payment
Under hire purchase the hirer becomes owner on paying the final instalment; under a lease the lessee never becomes owner
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
questions.explanation: In hire purchase, ownership passes to the person paying when the final instalment is paid. In a lease, the lessor remains owner and the lessee cannot become owner even after the lease period.
hints: Hire purchase does transfer ownership at the end.

questions.q: Account Aggregators in India are licensed by ____ and can share a customer's financial information:
options: RBI; only with the customer's express consent, which can be revoked at any time
RBI; without consent for loan applications
questions.explanation: Account aggregators are RBI-licensed entities that consolidate and share customer data with third parties only with express consent, and the customer may revoke consent at any time.
hints: Wrong regulator and consent is required.

questions.q: Which condition would prevent a company from making a bonus issue?
options: It has large free reserves from genuine profits
Its shares trade at a high price
Its board has approved the issue
It has defaulted on payment of interest or principal on its debt securities or fixed deposits
questions.explanation: A bonus issue is made out of free reserves built from genuine profits; a company that has defaulted on interest or principal on debt securities or fixed deposits cannot make one.
hints: Free reserves are the source of a bonus issue.
A high price is a reason for a split, not a bar to a bonus.
Board approval is a requirement, not a bar.

questions.q: Under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme, a resident individual can remit up to ____ per financial year for permissible current or capital account transactions.
questions.explanation: LRS allows resident individuals, including minors, to remit up to USD 2,50,000 per financial year. It started in 2004 with USD 25,000.
hints: This was the limit when LRS began in 2004.
USD 1 million relates to NRO repatriation, not LRS.

questions.q: A company pays a dividend of ₹6 per share and its share price is ₹150. If the price rises to ₹200 with the same dividend, the dividend yield will:
questions.explanation: Dividend yield = DPS / Price: 6/150 = 4% and 6/200 = 3%. A higher price lowers the yield.
hints: A higher denominator lowers the yield.

questions.q: A perpetual bond pays a coupon of ₹9 a year forever. If investors require a yield of 7.5%, its value is:
questions.explanation: Value of a perpetual bond = Coupon / Yield = 9 / 0.075 = ₹120.
hints: Par would apply only if yield equalled the coupon rate on ₹100.
This multiplies the coupon by the yield.

questions.q: Open interest in a futures contract refers to:
options: The number of contracts traded during the day
The interest rate built into the futures price
The margin deposited with the clearing corporation
The total number of outstanding contracts that have not been settled
questions.explanation: Open interest is the total number of outstanding derivative contracts not yet settled. It is not trading volume; rising open interest indicates money flowing into the market.
hints: That is volume, which the workbook distinguishes from open interest.

questions.q: A resident individual holds liquid fund units worth ₹40,000. Under the Instant Access Facility, the most she can receive instantly in a day is:
questions.explanation: IAF limit = lower of ₹50,000 or 90% of the latest value of investment, per day per scheme per investor. 90% of ₹40,000 = ₹36,000.
hints: The full value exceeds the 90% cap.
₹50,000 is higher than 90% of her holding, so the lower figure applies.

questions.q: A Fund of Funds scheme must invest at least ____ of its total assets in the underlying fund(s).
questions.explanation: As per the workbook, 95% of the total assets of a FoF should be invested in the underlying fund(s).
hints: 80% applies to large cap, sectoral and ELSS funds.

questions.q: An applicant seeking registration as a portfolio manager must have a net worth of:
questions.explanation: The SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations require the applicant to fulfil a net worth requirement of five crore rupees.
hints: ₹50 lakh is the minimum client investment.
₹20 crore is the minimum AIF scheme corpus.

questions.q: Which fund has the higher Sharpe ratio?
questions.explanation: Sharpe = (Rp - Rf) / σp. Alpha: (16 - 6) / 20 = 0.50. Beta: (13 - 6) / 12 = 0.583. Beta Fund is higher.
hints: Alpha's Sharpe is 0.50, but Beta's is higher.
This divides Alpha's total return by its standard deviation.
questions.case: Sanjay compares two equity funds over the same 3 years. Alpha Fund: annualised return 16%, standard deviation 20%, beta 1.1. Beta Fund: annualised return 13%, standard deviation 12%, beta 0.9. The risk-free rate is 6%.

questions.q: What is Alpha Fund's Treynor ratio?
questions.explanation: Treynor = (Rp - Rf) / β = (16 - 6) / 1.1 = 9.09 percentage points per unit of beta (0.0909).
hints: This divides total return by beta without subtracting Rf.
That is Beta Fund's Treynor ratio.
questions.case: Sanjay compares two equity funds over the same 3 years. Alpha Fund: annualised return 16%, standard deviation 20%, beta 1.1. Beta Fund: annualised return 13%, standard deviation 12%, beta 0.9. The risk-free rate is 6%.

questions.q: Sanjay's wealth is already held in well-diversified portfolios. Which measure should he use, and which fund does it favour?
questions.explanation: For a well-diversified investor only systematic risk matters, so Treynor is the appropriate measure. Treynor: Alpha 9.09 vs Beta (13 - 6) / 0.9 = 7.78, so Alpha Fund ranks higher.
hints: Sharpe suits an investor who is not well diversified.
Sharpe would not be the right measure, and it actually favours Beta Fund.
Treynor is right but Beta Fund's ratio (7.78) is lower.
questions.case: Sanjay compares two equity funds over the same 3 years. Alpha Fund: annualised return 16%, standard deviation 20%, beta 1.1. Beta Fund: annualised return 13%, standard deviation 12%, beta 0.9. The risk-free rate is 6%.

questions.q: A prospect offers a zero risk premium (a 'fair game'). A risk-averse investor will:
options: Accept it only if leverage is available
questions.explanation: Risk-averse investors reject fair games; they invest only in risk-free assets or in risky ones with a positive risk premium. Risk seekers would engage in a fair game; risk-neutral investors look only at expected return.
hints: Leverage is irrelevant to the definition.

questions.q: According to the studies cited in the workbook, for a single fund, asset allocation explains about ____ of the variation in its returns over time.
questions.explanation: Asset allocation explains about 90% of a single fund's return variation over time and about 40% of the variation across funds (Brinson, Hood and Beebower; Ibbotson and Kaplan).
hints: 40% is the figure across all funds.

questions.q: Which statement about investments made on behalf of a minor is correct?
options: The minor can have two adult joint holders
The guardian must be the first holder
A minor's account can continue to be operated by the guardian after the minor turns 18 without any change
The minor must be the sole (first) holder and there can be no joint holders
questions.explanation: Investments for a minor cannot have joint holders; the minor must be the sole or first holder, with the guardian transacting and completing KYC. On majority, transactions are frozen until the new major updates KYC.
hints: The minor, not the guardian, is the first holder.
Transactions are disallowed until KYC of the minor-turned-major is completed.

questions.q: An individual investment adviser must apply for registration as a non-individual IA when the number of clients exceeds ____ or the fee collected in a financial year exceeds ____, whichever is earlier.
questions.explanation: Individual IAs with more than 300 clients or fees exceeding ₹3 crore in a financial year must apply for in-principle registration as a non-individual IA (valid for 3 months to transition).
hints: 75 is the part-time IA client cap.

questions.q: An investment adviser uses an AI tool to generate portfolio recommendations. Under the IA Regulations as described in the workbook:
options: The AI vendor bears responsibility for any wrong advice
The IA is exempt from suitability rules for AI-generated advice
The IA is solely responsible for data security, confidentiality and the advice, and must disclose the extent of AI use to clients
AI use is prohibited for registered IAs
questions.explanation: An IA using AI tools, irrespective of scale, is solely responsible for client data security, confidentiality and integrity, the advice based on AI output, and legal compliance; it must also disclose the extent of AI use to clients.
hints: AI use is allowed, with responsibility and disclosure.

questions.q: Which of these is listed among SEBI's 'Don'ts' for investors dealing with investment advisers?
options: Do not ask for risk profiling
Do not pay fees through banking channels
Do not read the terms and conditions
Do not give your money for investment to the investment adviser
questions.explanation: SEBI advises investors not to give money for investment to the IA, not to fall for assured returns, stock tips or limited-period offers. Paying fees through banking channels and insisting on risk profiling are Do's.
hints: Insisting on risk profiling is a Do.
Paying via banking channels is a Do.
Reading terms carefully is a Do.

questions.q: If settlement by recommendation fails, the Insurance Ombudsman disposes of a complaint by passing an award within:
options: Three months from receipt of the complaint
questions.explanation: The Ombudsman first makes a recommendation within one month; if that fails, a speaking award is passed within 3 months from receipt of the complaint.
hints: One month is the timeline for the recommendation.
45 days is the SAT appeal window.

questions.q: A special situation fund, which invests in special situation assets and may act as a resolution applicant under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, is registered as a:
questions.explanation: The workbook lists special situation funds alongside venture capital, SME, social venture and infrastructure funds under Category I AIFs.
hints: Category II covers PE and debt funds without specific incentives.
Category III covers hedge funds using leverage and complex strategies.
This is an AIF structure, not a mutual fund.
